newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX seen extending surge after dollar boost.
newsitem.headline: German DAX seen extending surge after dollar boost.

text.p: German shares should continue their current rally, dealers said on Tuesday, as long as the dollar holds its gains and Wall Street ends firmer.
"We've had a huge run, but we remain bullish. Some investors had been holding back, but now they are being forced into the market," said one trader.
Dealers said the DAX index of 30 leading shares should penetrate the crucial 2,900 point level on Wednesday, if it did not make it in late computerised IBIS dealings.
The IBIS DAX was up 44.44 points, or 1.56 percent, at 2,897.90 points by 1545 GMT.
3-month high against the mark and strength in German government bonds, also at record highs, provided additional support for the market.

The U.S. currency surge came overnight following comments by Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing and New York Federal Reserve Bank William McDonough on the dollar becoming more important in the run up to European monetary union.
German export-oriented chemicals and auto companies were boosted by from dollar firmness, shares in BMW AG, Bayer AG and BASF AG leading the way.
BMW ended IBIS trade up almost six percent, or 59.30 marks, at 1,075.90 marks, while Bayer climbed five percent or 3.18 marks to 65.55 marks and BASF was up five percent to 60.88 marks.
Meanwhile shares in Volkswagen ended up 4.50 marks at 597.50 marks, as bargain hunters moved in to buy shares at lower prices.

In early dealings the stock had dropped over three percent to 574 marks, after a U.S. judge denied the firm's motion to dismiss General Motors Corp.'s remaining industrial espionage claims against the German carmaker.
